corrections.notes:
For the 12.5 cm Shawl Lapel shown in the image, the geometry differs fundamentally from a peak lapel because there is no gorge angle and no peak point. Instead, the collar and lapel form one continuous curve flowing from the neckline to the front edge.

Observed Features

The illustration shows:

Classic tuxedo-style shawl lapel
Continuous rounded outer edge
No notch or peak
Width approximately 12.5 cm
Symmetrical left/right geometry
Tapering toward the button stance
Primary Dimensions

W=12.5 cmW = 12.5\text{ cm}

C=4.0 cmC = 4.0\text{ cm}

Recommended roll radius:

R=1.4WR = 1.4W R=17.5 cmR = 17.5\text{ cm}
Drafting Geometry

A shawl lapel is typically drafted as a compound curve made from:

Upper collar arc
Outer roll arc
Front closing arc

The primary outer curve may be approximated by a circular arc:

x2+y2=R2x^2+y^2=R^2

For this width:

x2+y2=17.52x^2+y^2=17.5^2 x2+y2=306.25x^2+y^2=306.25

Finished Width       = 12.5 cm
Collar Width         = 4.0 cm
Outer Curve Radius   = 17.5 cm
Front Sweep Length   = 38-42 cm
Roll Line Depth      = 1.5 cm

Neck Point       (0.0, 0.0)

A fair curve through these points reproduces the profile shown in the illustration.

Style Characteristics

A 12.5 cm Shawl Lapel creates:

Strong formal tuxedo appearance
Broad chest emphasis
Continuous elegant roll
Softer appearance than peak lapels
Excellent proportions for dinner jackets and double-breasted tuxedos

A common bespoke rule is:

Outer Radius≈1.4×Lapel Width\text{Outer Radius} \approx 1.4 \times \text{Lapel Width}

so for a 12.5 cm shawl, a radius of roughly 17.5 cm gives a balanced and visually smooth curve matching the illustrated design.
